label: halloween-original
text:
Witches Hats-———€old-Black-
With the changing of the leaves
-and-their_tetting loose to float lazily _
to the ground, fall comes to Rap-
pahannock, in a burst of color and in
the aftermath, a bareness. “As the
wind scatters’ the dry leaves, a new
scent. pervades the air, and Hallo-
we’en with its witches, jack-o-lan-
terns, and scarry masks invades the
world of youth. It’s fun ‘cause it’s
dark and secret—you can shout and
blow horns and peep under crooked
masks. For one night you throw
inhibitions out. the window as you
are whirled into this make believe

environment.

Keep Pace. You're really old if
you can’t- summon a shiver at a
sheeted figure’s shrill “boo.” And the
housewife who ignores “tricks or
treats” is quickly and rightly classed
“an old fogey.”

But you fun-seekers—don’t carry
your jokes over the line. Respect an
individual’s rights—Hallowe’en does
not let down the bar in this respect.
Every year papers carry stories of
jokes turned tragedies because of a
moment of flight or a warped sense
of humor. Have fun in a legitimate
healthy way. Your neighbor likes to
laugh too.
tion when any desired changes in the
Constitution can be submitted to the
people from time to time as they ap-
pear. A “full dress” constitutional
convention would be enormously
costly and could change our whole
system of government without even
submitting the changes to the vote
of the people.
eee
